column3: Aggregates the product's overall resource efficiency into one score by combining its material efficiency (R1), energy efficiency (R2), and water efficiency (R3). Provides one figure to prioritize material-, energy-, and water-saving and circularity actions.
column4: To provide one single metric to prioritize material-saving and circularity actions.
column9: Sum (weight * R1 + weight * R2 + weight * R3)

column3: Aggregates the product's material-efficiency performance into one score by combining how much of the resource outflow is reutilized as material of value (R11) and how much of the product's mass is recoverable at end of life (R12). Higher means more material is kept in use and less becomes waste.
column4: To reduce material consumption and increase material reutilization.

column3: Measures the reutilization of the resource outflow that can be cycled as material of value within or outside the production process.
column4: To increase circular resource use and to reduce material waste.
column18: Org->product adaptation: the reutilization share concept is grounded in ISO 59020 A.3.3 (reused mass / total outflow mass), applied here at product level. ACM+17 source not in corpus; ISO 59020 is the retrievable ground.

column3: Measures the percentage of byproduct which is reused back into the product's lifecycle.

column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the share of the production's total byproduct outflow (R1-1) that is repurposed into another external product or system (R1-3). Higher means more outflow finds value outside the original lifecycle.
column4: To create value from outflows and reduce waste.
column9: Repurposed = Repurposed mass derived from outflow / Total mass of outflow\n\n(Repurposed - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the share of a product unit's mass that can be cycled back at end of life — reused, recycled, or repurposed — instead of becoming waste. Higher means more of the product is recoverable.
column4: To maximize the share of product mass that is recoverable at end of life.
column9: Recoverability = 1 - (Mass of Product Unit - Cyclable Potential) / Mass of Product Unit = Cyclable Potential / Mass of Product Unit
column18: End-of-Life Waste = (Mass of Product Unit - Cyclable Potential) / Mass — the product waste share, NORMALIZED against company Target Min/Max. 2026-06-25 (T3.6): folded in the former R121 (identical formula) and dropped the R1-5 reference-product-waste comparison (the Min/Max band already encodes the reference level); this removed the earlier kg-vs-share dimensional mismatch and its needs_review flag. | 2026-06-26: flipped direction (user decision). Was 'End-of-Life Waste' = (Mass - Cyclable)/Mass — a waste share (lower=better) that was never complemented, so it scored backwards under the higher=better normalization. Reformulated as the complement 1 - (Mass - Cyclable)/Mass = Cyclable/Mass = recoverable share (higher=better), renamed 'End-of-Life Recoverability', and seeded Min=0/Max=1 (now a bounded ratio; moved from PERFORMANCE_DIRECTION to SEED_01). See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md.

Aggregates the product's energy performance into one score by combining its energy-recovery performance (R21) and its energy-consumption performance (R22). Higher means more energy is recovered/reused and less is consumed per output across the product's life cycle.
column4: To provide an overview of current energy utilization metrics to prioritize energy-saving and circular energy actions.

column3: Measures how performant the energy recovery system of the product pipeline is. It evaluates the amount of energy that can be recovered from the non-circular resource outflow and how much of it is reused back into the product pipeline.
column18: Only applicable when there exist self-generated energy.

column3: Measures the overall energy generated from the resource outflow of the product's lifecycle.
column4: To capture value from outflows and improve energy circularity.
column9: Regen = Generated Energy / Potential Energy\n\n(Regen - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the percentage of generated energy in the product's lifecycle which is reused back into the process pipeline.
column4: To maximize reuse of energy with the goal of reducing purchased energy.
column9: Reuse = Recirculated Energy / Generated Energy\n\n(Reuse - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the share of recovered/generated energy (R2-2) that is put into storage rather than immediately reused — stored energy (R2-4) ÷ generated energy (R2-2), in any form (electricity, heat, etc.). Higher means more recovered energy is buffered for later use.
column9: Stored = Stored Energy / Generated Energy\n\n(Stored - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. See reviews/min-max-sourcing.md (T1.2).

column3: Measures the energy consumed per defined output (functional unit) across the product's lifecycle.
column4: To give an overview of current energy consumption metrics, reduce overall energy consumption, and enables benchmarking.

column3: Measures how efficiently the product converts supplied energy into useful output during the use phase — operational output energy (R2-5) ÷ operational input energy (R2-6). Higher means less energy is wasted to deliver the same product function.
column18: End User Energy Efficiency = Output/Input; a real ratio. Self-normalizes against company Target Min/Max. Re-tagged WEIGHTED_RATIO->NORMALIZED_RATIO 2026-06 (T3.6).

column3: Measures the energy consumption needed to produce or manufacture the products.

column18: Declines in energy intensity are a proxy for efficiency improvements.

Aggregates the product's water-efficiency performance into one score by combining its water-savings performance (R31, treatment + reuse), its water-consumption reduction over time (R32), and its water-utilization efficiency (R33, intake vs. discharge). column4: To provide an overview of current water utilization metrics to prioritize water-saving and circular water actions.

column4: To demonstrate effectiveness of water recovery and treatment efforts.

column3: Measures the share of processed / treated waste water into usable water.
column4: To increase the amount of water available for reuse and reduce freshwater consumption.
column9: Treated = Treated water from outflow / Total water outflow\n\n(Treated - Min) / (Max - Min)
column18: Min/Max seeded to default 0/1 — this ratio is already a 0-1 score; override only to score against a tighter target band. The total amount of water outflow that is reused or reutilized back as inflow in the product's lifecycle processes.
The total volume of water intake needed throughout the product's process cycle.
